title: The Honor Song for the Fallen

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A warrior from the village fell defending the far beach: sing the honor song, or mourn quietly as the family asks.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Word has come from the far beach: one of the village's warriors, (friend)'s brother, fell in the fight with the raiders. The warriors are bringing him home. (subject) knows the old honor song for those who fall defending the village. (friend) does not know if (friend.he/she) can bear a song that calls it an honor. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village sings the honor song on the beach as the canoe comes in. It is not a happy song. It is a song about what was lost. (friend) stands at the water's edge and does not sing, and nobody asks (friend.him/her) to. When it ends, (subject) stays beside (friend.him/her) until the sun goes down.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend)'s family asks for quiet, and the village gives it. There is no song, only a long line of people on the beach, each touching the canoe as it passes. Later, the warriors sing the honor song alone, far down the shore, where the family cannot hear.
